text.p: These are the leading stories in the Namibian press on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- After the Uutapi magistrate's court in northern Namibia cleared the deputy minister of environment and tourism, Nangolo Ithete, of illegally purchasing ostriches and ostrich eggs, it is now likely that three witnesses will be charged with perjury. - The Namibian Legal Assistance Center is to apply for the lowering of a N$200 bail imposed on the 19 San-protesters still in police custody after Sunday's demonstration at Etosha National Park.
- Another Namibian has announced in public that she has contracted the HIV virus.
- A 35-year-old mother has made public that she is HIV positive, urging Namibians to be aware of the existence of the disease and the fact that anyone can contract it if they do not live responsibly.

- Heavy rainfall in southern Namibia has filled Namibia's biggest reservoir the Hardap dam at Mariental to its highest level for years, with the Fish River flowing in full width. The dam was filled to 43 percent of its capacity while the figure stood at only 11.8 percent on Monday with further inflows expected.
